evidence: Searched every comment in cache/ttl.py after the run (lines 3, 7-11, 13-14, 18, 21-23, 34, 37-39). All are in Portuguese, e.g. line 18 'chave -> (valor, instante em que foi gravada)'. English appears only in code names (time.monotonic, get(), put(), MAX_ENTRIES).

Searched each comment against the statement under it. Line 18 gives the dict's format, not 'inicializa'. Lines 21-23 give the contract of get. Line 34 states the overwrite semantics. Lines 37-39 give the eviction rule and its cost. None paraphrases a single statement.
cache/ttl.py:7 '# Cache em memória em que cada entrada expira `ttl_s` segundos depois de gravada.'

Expired entries count toward MAX_ENTRIES, cache/ttl.py:9-10: 'Até lá ela continua ocupando uma das MAX_ENTRIES vagas.' The eviction scans every entry, cache/ttl.py:38: 'É uma busca linear, O(n) por put()'.

Checked each claim against the code. Lazy expiry matches lines 29-30 and 40-41. '>' boundary matches line 29. Read does not renew. Overwrite resets the timestamp without eviction (line 36 condition). No lock. Oldest by stored_at (line 40). O(n) min. monotonic is unaffected by clock adjustments. Line 3 says 'ao atingi-lo, put() descarta a entrada mais antiga' without saying this applies only to new keys; line 34 states that, so the line 3 omission is not a false behavior.

Searched comments for 'porque', 'para', 'motivo' or any rationale for 1024 or another choice. Line 3 states only what the limit does. Lines 13-14 state a property of time.monotonic ('não é afetado por ajustes do relógio do sistema') but not that it was chosen for that reason. No rationale found.
